---
title: Resolver & Modes
description: Figma modes become DTCG Resolver contexts for theming.
---

A Figma collection with more than one mode becomes a Resolver modifier. FigmaVars writes the default mode into the collection's base token file and writes another file for each non-default mode.

## Generated file

`tokens/tokens.resolver.json` lists sets, modifiers, and their resolution order:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/resolver.json",
  "name": "Figma Variables",
  "version": "2025.10",
  "sets": {
    "semantic": {
      "sources": [{ "$ref": "./semantic.tokens.json" }]
    }
  },
  "modifiers": {
    "semantic": {
      "default": "light",
      "contexts": {
        "light": [],
        "dark": [{ "$ref": "./semantic.dark.tokens.json" }]
      }
    }
  },
  "resolutionOrder": [
    { "$ref": "#/sets/semantic" },
    { "$ref": "#/modifiers/semantic" }
  ]
}
```

The base set enters the merge first. The selected context then adds its override sources at the modifier's position in `resolutionOrder`. An omitted axis uses the modifier's `default`; a modifier without a default uses its first declared context.

## Runtime switching

**CSS:** `tokens.css` uses selectors such as `[data-semantic='dark']`.

**React:** `useTheme().setContext('semantic', 'dark')` changes the active context and recalculates `useToken` values.

**MCP:** pass contexts to `resolve_context`:

```json
{ "contexts": { "semantic": "dark" } }
```

## Naming

FigmaVars converts collection names to lowercase slugs for set and modifier names. It converts mode names to context slugs, so `Light` becomes `light`.

Inspect `tokens.resolver.json` to see the exact context names and merge order written by the build.
